checks.detail: PASS: benchmark artifact matches a fresh execution
checks.name: benchmark_reproducible

summary: 8/8 required checks pass on a fresh run in this session. Independent adversarial testing (13 scenarios in throwaway clones) found the git-layer enforcement real for ordinary violations (7/7 caught: verifier writing scripts/, verifier writing state/claims.jsonl, missing trailers, unknown session, unheld role, edited state line, deleted state file); R3/R4/R5 hold at the state layer (self-review, append-only, git-blame authorship binding all rejected). Four gaps remain that the standard suite cannot detect: F1 (High) Session-Id is self-declared and the branch binding is checked for HEAD only, so a commit forging another session's identity passes check-all (demonstrated: the guard itself weakened under a forged bootstrap identity, check-all ok=true); F2 (High) merge commits are skipped and --first-parent excludes side-branch commits, so scripts/ and .github/ can be landed with no trailers and no proposal (demonstrated, check-all ok=true); F3 (Medium) "check-commits --stage land" is not a CLI argument, so CI's land gate exits 2 with a usage error - called programmatically it is vacuous for merge commits and misattributes every file to the verifier for squash merges; F4 (Medium) "researchos_session.py close" on your own session makes check-commits fail with "session is closed". Also: RQ-001 lists a required check "governance_review" that the suite never emits (it emits "policy"), and required_checks are never compared against a review's checks; the verifier may rewrite gitswarm/artifacts/readout_snapshot.json, so readout_snapshot proves only "no drift since the last verifier re-baseline". Verdict: pass with conditions. "pass" means the 8 required checks passed, not that the harness is gap-free. F1-F4 must be closed by a follow-up proposal (PRP-002) before this harness is treated as a hard gate; until then the merge to main remains the human gate of record.
